turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Good afternoon, I'm Dr. Shah. Come, sit down. Your husband can wait outside for a bit, and we'll call him if you like.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, let him wait. I... I don't know, doctor, I'm very scared.
[SEG0003] person_1 (DOCTOR): That's alright, take your time. What has been happening?
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): I'm pregnant, I think eight or ten weeks, and there is spotting, and cramps also, like my periods.
[SEG0005] person_1 (DOCTOR): When was your last proper period?
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): The spotting is brown, doctor, not bright red. In the morning it looks a little pink sometimes.
[SEG0007] person_1 (DOCTOR): We'll note the colour, but I still need the period date. Can you place the last one?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): I don't know, doctor. It was around Diwali, or after Diwali. I'm not sure which.
[SEG0009] person_1 (DOCTOR): No problem. Was there any bleeding after that period, before this spotting started?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): No, nothing in between. Then this spotting came, and I don't know from when. Since Diwali or after, something like that. I keep mixing it up.
[SEG0011] person_1 (DOCTOR): Where do you feel the cramps?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): Low down, both sides. Like period pain. Not the whole stomach.
[SEG0013] person_1 (DOCTOR): How many pads have you used since this morning?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): My mother keeps phoning. She says lie down, drink coconut water, don't go anywhere. I don't know, doctor, I'm just frightened something is wrong with the baby.
[SEG0015] person_1 (DOCTOR): Mothers do that. Still, the pads — since morning, how many, and were they soaked?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): Um, only one pad, and it's not soaked, just spots. No clots... well, actually, I thought there was a small clot yesterday, but no, it was only thick brown, not a clot.
[SEG0017] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any giddiness, any fainting, any pain in the shoulder?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): No giddiness. I didn't faint. Shoulder is fine.
[SEG0019] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any fever, or burning when you pass urine?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): No fever. Urine is normal, no burning.
[SEG0021] person_1 (DOCTOR): What about nausea or vomiting?
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): Nausea is there, mostly in the mornings. I haven't vomited. I don't know if it's the pregnancy or just the worry.
[SEG0023] person_1 (DOCTOR): And sleep?
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): Very bad. I was awake half the night, not really from the pain, from thinking too much.
[SEG0025] person_1 (DOCTOR): What tablets are you on?
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): Folic acid, five milligrams, once a day, since the test was positive. And thyroxine, for my thyroid.
[SEG0027] person_1 (DOCTOR): What strength of thyroxine, and how do you take it?
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): Every morning, on an empty stomach. The dose, I don't know, doctor. Maybe seventy-five micrograms. They changed it once. I get confused.
[SEG0029] person_1 (DOCTOR): Anything else, even for pain? Anything you have stopped?
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): I used to take mefenamic acid for period pain, two hundred and fifty milligrams. I stopped it when the test came positive. Not a single tablet after that.
[SEG0031] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any allergy, to a medicine or a food?
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Nothing like that.
[SEG0033] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any illness we should know about, apart from the thyroid?

[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): Thyroid only. It started last winter, or the one before, I can't remember. It's still there. I take the tablet daily, I think, most days. Sometimes I forget on Sundays. I don't know.
[SEG0035] person_1 (DOCTOR): So the thyroid problem is ongoing, and a few Sunday doses may be getting missed. Any operation in the past?
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): No operation.
[SEG0037] person_1 (DOCTOR): Do you smoke, or drink alcohol?
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): Never smoked. No alcohol. I'm a primary teacher, on leave now. We live with my in-laws, so the house is never quiet.
[SEG0039] person_1 (DOCTOR): Let me just check. Blood pressure is one hundred and eight over sixty-eight. Pulse is ninety-two. Temperature is thirty-seven point one.
[SEG0040] person_1 (DOCTOR): Your tummy is soft. There is mild tenderness across the lower abdomen. No guarding, and no rigidity.
[SEG0041] person_2 (PATIENT): It hurts a little when you press, yes. Only a little.
[SEG0042] person_1 (DOCTOR): Shall we call your husband in, so he hears the plan as well?
[SEG0043] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, call him. He is sitting just outside, he was complaining about the parking earlier.
[SEG0044] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Sorry, the parking is a nightmare out there. She has been very unwell. The pain is bad, she was crying with it since yesterday, she could not even lie straight.
[SEG0045] person_2 (PATIENT): No, Arjun, it's not like that. The pain is like periods, I can manage. I was crying because I am scared, not because the pain is so bad.
[SEG0046] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): And the spotting, doctor, it has been two weeks. She told me two weeks.
[SEG0047] person_2 (PATIENT): I didn't say two weeks for sure. Maybe three weeks, or two, I don't know, doctor. It was around Diwali, or after. I can't put a date on it.
[SEG0048] person_1 (DOCTOR): Right. So he says two weeks, you say two or three weeks, and the actual day is still around Diwali or after. I won't lock a date.
[SEG0049] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Her thyroxine is a hundred micrograms. I saw that on the strip last month.
[SEG0050] person_2 (PATIENT): That was the old strip. I think the new one is seventy-five. I don't know, doctor, I didn't bring the box.
[SEG0051] person_1 (DOCTOR): Then I won't guess the dose. Bring the strip with you next time. Apart from some Sundays, are you still taking it every morning?
[SEG0052] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, mornings, except some Sundays. I don't know how many I missed.
[SEG0053] person_1 (DOCTOR): I can't be sure today what this is. It may be a threatened miscarriage, or it may only be spotting in early pregnancy. We need the tests before saying more.
[SEG0054] person_1 (DOCTOR): Today we'll do a scan, a transvaginal ultrasound if you're agreeable, and blood tests — haemoglobin, blood group, and a serum beta-hCG.
[SEG0055] person_2 (PATIENT): A scan today? Will it harm the baby? I don't know, doctor.
[SEG0056] person_1 (DOCTOR): It won't harm the baby. It shows us if the pregnancy is inside the uterus and if there is a heartbeat. Please have the blood tests and the scan today, before you leave.
[SEG0057] person_2 (PATIENT): Okay. For the cramps, can I take something?

[SEG0058] person_1 (DOCTOR): Start paracetamol, five hundred milligrams by mouth, three times a day, for the cramps, for the next few days. Don't take mefenamic acid or ibuprofen. Keep taking the folic acid, five milligrams, once a day.

[SEG0059] person_1 (DOCTOR): I want to see you back in this clinic in three days, with the reports. If you soak a pad within one hour, or you feel giddy, or the pain becomes severe, come back straight away, don't wait.
[SEG0060] person_2 (PATIENT): Three days, and if it gets heavy or I feel giddy, come immediately. I understand. I'm still very worried.
[SEG0061] person_1 (DOCTOR): Of course you are. One step at a time. Reception will send you for the bloods and the scan now, and I'll see you in three days, sooner if those signs show up.
